questions.sec: Definition of CKD & the causes table · p793
questions.q: Chronic kidney disease in this chapter is defined histologically by more than what percentage of interstitial fibrosis, tubular atrophy or glomerular sclerosis?
questions.exp: CKD: >5% of interstitial fibrosis/tubular atrophy/glomerular sclerosis, with a decrease in the number of functional nephrons. (Book p793)

questions.sec: Definition of CKD & the causes table · p793
questions.q: Fill up: CKD is characterised by a ______ in the number of functional nephrons.
questions.exp: CKD definition: >5% interstitial fibrosis/tubular atrophy/glomerular sclerosis with ↓ number of functional nephrons. (Book p793)

questions.sec: Definition of CKD & the causes table · p793
questions.q: Match each pathology with its associated condition in the causes table — 1) Vascular  2) Glomerular (diabetes)  3) Tubulo-interstitial fibrosis … A) Diabetic nephropathy  B) Ischemic nephropathy  C) CTID
questions.exp: Causes table: vascular (RAS, TMA) → ischemic nephropathy; glomerular (diabetes) → diabetic nephropathy; tubulo-interstitial fibrosis (–) → CTID. (Book p793)

questions.sec: Definition of CKD & the causes table · p793
questions.q: A patient has renal artery stenosis and biopsy shows ischaemic nephropathy. In the causes table, this belongs to which pathology group?
questions.exp: Vascular pathology (RAS, TMA) leads to ischemic nephropathy, and together with the glomerular group it produces secondary tubulo-interstitial fibrosis. (Book p793)

questions.sec: Definition of CKD & the causes table · p793
questions.q: Which glomerular diseases are grouped together with IgA nephropathy to cause chronic glomerulonephritis (CGN)?
opts: RAS and TMA, producing ischaemic nephropathy
Diabetes mellitus and hypertension, causing diabetic nephropathy
Sarcoidosis and Sjögren's syndrome, causing interstitial infiltration
questions.exp: Glomerular row of the causes table: IgA/MPGN/FSGS/membranous nephropathy → CGN (chronic glomerulonephritis). (Book p793)

questions.sec: Definition of CKD & the causes table · p793
questions.q: Match each cause of CKD with its label in the table — 1) IgAN/MPGN/FSGS/membranous nephropathy  2) Diabetes  3) RAS/TMA … A) Diabetic nephropathy  B) CGN (chronic glomerulonephritis)  C) Ischemic nephropathy
questions.exp: Table mapping: IgAN/MPGN/FSGS/membranous → CGN; diabetes → diabetic nephropathy; RAS/TMA → ischaemic nephropathy; primary tubulointerstitial fibrosis → CTID. (Book p793)

questions.sec: Definition of CKD & the causes table · p793
questions.q: In the causes table, vascular and glomerular pathology together are grouped as producing secondary tubulo-interstitial fibrosis.
opts: False — only vascular disease produces tubulointerstitial fibrosis
False — the grouping is labelled primary fibrosis
True, but only when diabetes is absent
questions.exp: The brace in the table labels the vascular and glomerular rows as 'secondary tubulo-interstitial fibrosis', leaving primary tubulo-interstitial fibrosis as CTID. (Book p793)

questions.sec: Definition of CKD & the causes table · p793
questions.q: All but one of the following are listed as conditions associated with CKD in the causes table. Which is the odd one out?
opts: IgA nephropathy, MPGN, FSGS and membranous nephropathy
questions.exp: The associated conditions listed are RAS/TMA, IgAN/MPGN/FSGS/membranous nephropathy and diabetes; PSGN is a self-limited disease not listed here. (Book p793)

questions.sec: CTID pathology & etiology (ciliopathies to metabolic) · p793
questions.q: The pathology of chronic tubulointerstitial disease is:
opts: Scarring with tubulointerstitial fibrosis and atrophy of more than 5%
Segmental sclerosis of the glomerular tuft only
questions.exp: Pathology of CTID: scarring + tubulointerstitial fibrosis & atrophy (>5%), illustrated by the histopathology figure. (Book p793)

questions.sec: CTID pathology & etiology (ciliopathies to metabolic) · p793
questions.q: Which of the following is the first listed etiology of chronic tubulointerstitial disease?
questions.exp: The etiology list begins with ciliopathies, followed by reflux nephropathy (VUR), obstructive nephropathy, drugs, toxins and metabolic causes. (Book p793)

questions.sec: CTID pathology & etiology (ciliopathies to metabolic) · p793
questions.q: Fill up: Reflux nephropathy, listed second among the etiologies, is due to ______.
questions.exp: Etiology 2 of CTID: reflux nephropathy (VUR — vesicoureteric reflux). (Book p793)

questions.sec: CTID pathology & etiology (ciliopathies to metabolic) · p793
questions.q: Match each drug with its characteristic CTID lesion — 1) Lithium  2) Calcineurin inhibitors  3) Proton pump inhibitors … A) Striped pattern with afferent arteriolar hyalinosis  B) Microcystic changes in distal tubules without interstitial inflammation  C) Listed as a drug causing CTID
questions.exp: Drugs in CTID: lithium — microcystic changes in distal tubules without interstitial inflammation; calcineurin inhibitors — striped pattern, afferent arteriolar hyalinosis; PPIs also listed. (Book p793)

questions.sec: CTID pathology & etiology (ciliopathies to metabolic) · p793
questions.q: A patient on long-term lithium develops renal impairment. The biopsy is expected to show:
opts: Microcystic changes in distal tubules without interstitial inflammation
Striped pattern of fibrosis with afferent arteriolar hyalinosis
questions.exp: Lithium: microcystic changes in distal tubules without interstitial inflammation. The striped pattern with afferent arteriolar hyalinosis is a calcineurin-inhibitor effect. (Book p793)

questions.sec: CTID pathology & etiology (ciliopathies to metabolic) · p793
questions.q: A renal transplant recipient on tacrolimus has progressive renal dysfunction. The characteristic histological pattern is:
opts: Striped pattern with afferent arteriolar hyalinosis
Microcystic change in distal tubules without inflammation
questions.exp: Calcineurin inhibitors (–) produce a striped pattern with afferent arteriolar hyalinosis. (Book p793)

questions.sec: CTID pathology & etiology (ciliopathies to metabolic) · p793
questions.q: Match each toxin with its CTID syndrome — 1) Lead  2) Cadmium … A) Ouch Ouch nephropathy  B) Saturnine gout with hyperuricemia
questions.exp: Toxins: lead — saturnine gout with hyperuricemia; cadmium — ouch ouch nephropathy. (Book p793)

questions.sec: CTID pathology & etiology (ciliopathies to metabolic) · p793
questions.q: Fill up: Cadmium toxicity causes the so-called ______ nephropathy.
questions.exp: Toxins in CTID: lead — saturnine gout/hyperuricemia; cadmium — 'ouch ouch nephropathy'. (Book p793)

questions.sec: CTID pathology & etiology (ciliopathies to metabolic) · p793
questions.q: A battery-recycling worker has gout with hyperuricemia and renal impairment. Which toxin is implicated?
questions.exp: Lead causes saturnine gout with hyperuricemia; cadmium causes ouch ouch nephropathy. (Book p793)

questions.sec: CTID pathology & etiology (ciliopathies to metabolic) · p793
questions.q: Match the metabolic cause of CTID with its named entity — 1) Hyperuricemia  2) Hypokalemia … A) Vacuolization of PCT > DCT  B) Urate nephropathy
questions.exp: Metabolic causes of CTID: hypercalcemia, hyperuricemia (urate nephropathy), hyperoxaluria and hypokalemia (vacuolization of PCT > DCT). (Book p793)

questions.sec: CTID pathology & etiology (ciliopathies to metabolic) · p793
questions.q: Hypokalemia in CTID produces vacuolization of the proximal convoluted tubule more than the distal convoluted tubule.
opts: False — vacuolization affects the DCT more than the PCT
False — hypokalemia causes no tubular change
True, but only when hypercalcemia coexists
questions.exp: Metabolic etiology list: hypokalemia — vacuolization of PCT > DCT. (Book p793)

questions.sec: CTID pathology & etiology (ciliopathies to metabolic) · p793
questions.q: The histology figures for urate nephropathy and for IgG4 disease in this section both carry an arrow pointing to:
opts: Fibrosis, with the disease name printed beneath each figure
Tubular atrophy, with glomerular sparing noted in the label
An interstitial infiltrate, with normal glomeruli in both panels
Basket-weave lamellation of the lamina densa on electron microscopy
questions.exp: The histology figures are labelled CTID histopathology (fibrosis, tubular atrophy), urate nephropathy (fibrosis) and IgG4 disease (fibrosis). (Book p793)

questions.sec: CTID pathology & etiology (ciliopathies to metabolic) · p793
questions.q: All but one of the following are listed causes of chronic tubulointerstitial disease. Which is the odd one out?
questions.exp: Listed etiologies: ciliopathies, reflux nephropathy (VUR), obstructive nephropathy, drugs, toxins and metabolic causes plus autoimmune diseases. (Book p793)

questions.sec: Autoimmune etiology, features & clinical-features table · p794
questions.q: Match the autoimmune causes of CTID — 1) Sarcoidosis  2) Sjögren's  3) IgG4 disease … A) All three are autoimmune causes listed  B) None is a cause
opts: All three are listed autoimmune causes
Only IgG4 disease is a cause
questions.exp: Autoimmune causes of CTID: sarcoidosis, Sjögren's and IgG4 disease (the last shown in the histology figure). (Book p794)

questions.sec: Autoimmune etiology, features & clinical-features table · p794
questions.q: Fill up: The last entry in the etiology list of CTID is CKDu, which stands for CKD of ______.
questions.exp: Etiology 8: CKD u (unknown) — CKD of unknown cause, discussed later as CKDu. (Book p794)

questions.sec: Autoimmune etiology, features & clinical-features table · p794
questions.q: CTID is described as having which onset?
questions.exp: Features of CTID: asymptomatic, insidious onset — hence patients often present late. (Book p794)

questions.sec: Autoimmune etiology, features & clinical-features table · p794
questions.q: A patient with CTID has polyuria and nocturia. The table explains this by:
questions.exp: Clinical-features table: polyuria and nocturia arise from a defect in concentration capacity. (Book p794)

questions.sec: Autoimmune etiology, features & clinical-features table · p794
questions.q: Anaemia in chronic tubulointerstitial disease is caused by damage to:
opts: Erythropoietin produced from peritubular interstitial fibroblasts
Erythropoietin produced by the glomerular mesangium
Erythropoietin produced by the proximal tubular brush border
questions.exp: Anaemia row of the table: erythropoietin is produced from peritubular interstitial fibroblasts, which are damaged in CTID. (Book p794)

questions.sec: Autoimmune etiology, features & clinical-features table · p794
questions.q: Match the tubular lesion with the resulting syndrome in the table — 1) Cortical collecting duct fibrosis  2) β cell fibrosis  3) α intercalated cell fibrosis … A) RTA I  B) Nephrogenic DI (↓ADH action)  C) RTA IV/pseudohypoaldosteronism (↓Aldosterone action)
questions.exp: Clinical-features table: cortical collecting duct fibrosis → ↓ADH action = nephrogenic DI; β cell fibrosis → ↓aldosterone action = RTA IV (pseudohypoaldosteronism); α intercalated cell fibrosis → RTA I. (Book p794)

questions.sec: Autoimmune etiology, features & clinical-features table · p794
questions.q: A patient with CTID has hyperkalemia, metabolic acidosis and low aldosterone effect, and is labelled as pseudohypoaldosteronism. Which lesion and type of RTA is this?
opts: β cell fibrosis causing RTA IV
α intercalated cell fibrosis causing RTA I
Cortical collecting duct fibrosis causing nephrogenic DI
questions.exp: RTA IV (pseudohypoaldosteronism) results from β cell fibrosis with ↓aldosterone action; RTA I results from α intercalated cell fibrosis. (Book p794)

questions.sec: Autoimmune etiology, features & clinical-features table · p794
questions.q: Nephrogenic diabetes insipidus in CTID is due to fibrosis of the cortical collecting duct reducing ADH action.
opts: False — it is due to central ADH deficiency
False — it is due to α intercalated cell fibrosis
questions.exp: Table: nephrogenic DI — cortical collecting duct fibrosis → ↓ADH action. (Book p794)

questions.sec: Autoimmune etiology, features & clinical-features table · p794
questions.q: A child with CTID has severe rickets. The table attributes this to:
questions.exp: Children with CTID develop severe ricketic features due to loss of PO₄³⁻. (Book p794)

questions.sec: Autoimmune etiology, features & clinical-features table · p794
questions.q: Match the anaemia severity with the CKD condition — 1) Maximum anaemia  2) Minimum anaemia … A) AD-PKD  B) CTID
questions.exp: Note: anaemia in CKD is maximum in CTID and minimum in AD-PKD (EPO production preserved in ADPKD). (Book p794)

questions.sec: Autoimmune etiology, features & clinical-features table · p794
questions.q: Among the causes of CKD, CTID is associated with the maximum anaemia and ADPKD with the minimum.
opts: False — ADPKD has the maximum anaemia
False — anaemia is equal in all causes
True, but only after dialysis starts
questions.exp: Note: anaemia in CKD — maximum in CTID, minimum in AD-PKD. (Book p794)

questions.sec: Autoimmune etiology, features & clinical-features table · p794
questions.q: All but one of the following are listed autoimmune causes of CTID. Which is the odd one out?
questions.exp: Autoimmune list for CTID: sarcoidosis, Sjögren's and IgG4 disease; anti-GBM disease causes RPGN. (Book p794)

questions.sec: CTID investigations & CKDu concept · p794
questions.q: The proteinuria of chronic tubulointerstitial disease is typically:
opts: Less than 2 g/day, with β₂ microglobulin in the urine
More than 3.5 g/day, in the nephrotic range, with oedema
Between 2 and 3 g/day, with RBC casts in the sediment
Absent in all cases, despite significant tubular damage
questions.exp: Urine in CTID: proteinuria <2 g/day (β₂ microglobulin) — a tubular pattern, not nephrotic range. (Book p794)

questions.sec: CTID investigations & CKDu concept · p794
questions.q: The urinary sediment in CTID is described as:
questions.exp: Urine in CTID: proteinuria <2 g/day (β₂ microglobulin) and inactive urinary sediments. (Book p794)

questions.sec: CTID investigations & CKDu concept · p794
questions.q: Match each CTID investigation with its finding — 1) Urine protein  2) Urinary sediment  3) RFT  4) USG … A) B/L small kidneys  B) <2 g/day with β₂ microglobulin  C) Deranged  D) Inactive
questions.exp: CTID investigations: urine — proteinuria <2 g/day (β₂ microglobulin) with inactive sediments; RFT deranged; USG — bilateral small kidneys. (Book p794)

questions.sec: CTID investigations & CKDu concept · p794
questions.q: An ultrasound in a patient with CTID typically shows:
questions.exp: USG in CTID: B/L small kidneys — the shrunken kidney of chronic tubulointerstitial fibrosis. (Book p794)

questions.sec: CTID investigations & CKDu concept · p794
questions.q: Fill up: The tubular protein marker raised in the urine of CTID is ______ microglobulin.
questions.exp: Urine in CTID: proteinuria <2 g/day with β₂ microglobulin, indicating tubular proteinuria. (Book p794)

questions.sec: CTID investigations & CKDu concept · p794
questions.q: Regarding the pathophysiology of CKDu (CKD of unknown etiology), the book states:
opts: It is unknown, with theories proposed and no precipitating disease
It is caused by diabetes mellitus in all cases, with diabetic retinopathy
It is an inherited ciliopathy with multiple bilateral renal cysts on imaging
It is due to recurrent urinary tract infection with chronic pyelonephritis
questions.exp: CKDu pathophysiology: unknown, theories proposed, and no precipitating disease. (Book p794)

questions.sec: CTID investigations & CKDu concept · p794
questions.q: CKDu is defined by the presence of a clear precipitating disease such as diabetes or hypertension.
opts: False — by definition no precipitating disease is present
True — diabetic nephropathy is the usual precipitant
False — CKDu always follows lithium therapy
questions.exp: CKDu: pathophysiology unknown, theories proposed, and no precipitating disease. (Book p794)

questions.sec: CTID investigations & CKDu concept · p794
questions.q: All but one of the following are stated about CTID. Which is the odd one out?
opts: Nephrotic-range proteinuria with active urinary sediment
questions.exp: CTID has subnephrotic proteinuria (<2 g/day) with inactive sediments and small kidneys. Nephrotic-range proteinuria with an active sediment indicates glomerular disease. (Book p794)

questions.sec: CKDu theories flowchart, epidemiology & clinical features · p795
questions.q: Match each proposed CKDu factor with its place in the flowchart — 1) Heat stress  2) Agrochemicals  3) Fluoride in ground water … A) All arrow into CKDu interstitial fibrosis  B) None relates to CKDu
opts: All three are proposed contributors to CKDu
Only heat stress contributes, the others being unrelated
Only agrochemicals contribute to the fibrosis and tubular atrophy
None of these three factors appears in the CKDu flowchart
questions.exp: Proposed theories for CKDu (→ interstitial fibrosis & tubular atrophy): heat stress, agrochemicals and fluoride in ground water, with heavy metals (cadmium) and communicable disease from the right. (Book p795)

questions.sec: CKDu theories flowchart, epidemiology & clinical features · p795
questions.q: Match the right-sided contributors to CKDu — 1) Heavy metals  2) Communicable disease … A) Example given is cadmium  B) Also listed as a proposed factor
questions.exp: CKDu flowchart right side: heavy metals — e.g. cadmium — and communicable disease. (Book p795)

questions.sec: CKDu theories flowchart, epidemiology & clinical features · p795
questions.q: A middle-aged man from the eastern coast of India, working as a farmer in the heat, presents with renal failure without diabetes or hypertension. Which entity fits?
opts: CKDu — CKD of unknown etiology, reported on the eastern coast of India in middle-aged men
Diabetic kidney disease, presenting with heavy proteinuria and diabetic retinopathy
Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease with bilateral enlarged cystic kidneys
Medullary sponge kidney presenting with recurrent stones and nephrocalcinosis
questions.exp: CKDu epidemiology: eastern coast of India, middle-aged men, with no precipitating disease. (Book p795)

questions.sec: CKDu theories flowchart, epidemiology & clinical features · p795
questions.q: Fill up: CKDu is reported on the ______ coast of India and in middle-aged men.
questions.exp: Epidemiology of CKDu: eastern coast of India, middle-aged men. (Book p795)

questions.sec: CKDu theories flowchart, epidemiology & clinical features · p795
questions.q: CKDu is described as asymptomatic until:
opts: The serum creatinine value has doubled
questions.exp: CKDu box: asymptomatic until ESRF — edema and hypertension are late features, proteinuria is absent or mild. (Book p795)

questions.sec: CKDu theories flowchart, epidemiology & clinical features · p795
questions.q: In CKDu, oedema and hypertension are late features rather than early ones.
opts: False — oedema and hypertension are the earliest features
False — oedema never occurs in CKDu
questions.exp: CKDu box: asymptomatic until ESRF, with oedema and hypertension as late features. (Book p795)

questions.sec: CKDu theories flowchart, epidemiology & clinical features · p795
questions.q: Match each CKDu box finding — 1) Proteinuria  2) Tubular biomarkers  3) Outcome … A) Elevated  B) Absent/mild  C) ESRF
questions.exp: CKDu box: absent/mild proteinuria, elevated tubular biomarkers, and progression to ESRF. (Book p795)

questions.sec: CKDu theories flowchart, epidemiology & clinical features · p795
questions.q: A patient from an endemic CKDu area has a normal urine dipstick for protein but a raised tubular biomarker. Which statement from the flowchart explains this?
opts: CKDu causes absent/mild proteinuria with elevated tubular biomarkers
CKDu always causes nephrotic-range proteinuria with generalised oedema
Tubular biomarkers fall early while proteinuria appears later in CKDu
Proteinuria is the first manifestation, appearing long before renal failure
questions.exp: CKDu box: absent/mild proteinuria, elevated tubular biomarkers, and progression to ESRF. (Book p795)

questions.sec: CKDu theories flowchart, epidemiology & clinical features · p795
questions.q: All but one of the following are proposed in the CKDu theories flowchart. Which is the odd one out?
questions.exp: CKDu theories: heat stress, agrochemicals, fluoride in ground water, heavy metals (cadmium) and communicable disease; NSAIDs are not in this flowchart. (Book p795)

questions.sec: CKDu theories flowchart, epidemiology & clinical features · p795
questions.q: The clinical features of CKDu given in the box are:
questions.exp: Clinical features of CKDu: anemia + proteinuria. (Book p795)

questions.sec: CKDu theories flowchart, epidemiology & clinical features · p795
questions.q: Fill up: The clinical features of CKDu listed are anemia and ______.
questions.exp: CKDu clinical features: anemia + proteinuria, illustrating that tubular-interstitial damage produces anaemia early. (Book p795)

questions.sec: CKDu theories flowchart, epidemiology & clinical features · p795
questions.q: A 45-year-old farmer from the eastern coast of India is found to have ESRF with only mild proteinuria and no diabetes or hypertension. Which statement is most consistent with CKDu?
opts: The disease is asymptomatic until ESRF, with oedema and hypertension as late features
The disease presents early with nephrotic-range proteinuria and generalised oedema
The disease is a hereditary ciliopathy with multiple bilateral renal cysts
The disease always begins in childhood with rickets and growth failure
questions.exp: CKDu: no precipitating disease, asymptomatic until ESRF, with oedema/hypertension as late features and absent or mild proteinuria. (Book p795)

units.title: CKD definition and the causes of chronic tubulointerstitial disease
units.guide: CKD = >5% interstitial fibrosis/tubular atrophy/glomerular sclerosis with fewer functional nephrons. The causes table maps vascular (RAS/TMA), glomerular (IgAN/MPGN/FSGS/membranous and diabetes) causes to secondary tubulointerstitial fibrosis, and primary tubulointerstitial fibrosis to CTID. Pathology is scarring with fibrosis and atrophy >5%.

units.title: Etiology of CTID: from ciliopathies to metabolic and autoimmune causes
units.guide: Etiology runs from ciliopathies, reflux nephropathy (VUR) and obstructive nephropathy, through drugs (lithium microcysts; calcineurin-inhibitor striped pattern with afferent arteriolar hyalinosis; PPIs) and toxins (lead saturnine gout; cadmium ouch ouch nephropathy) to metabolic causes (hypercalcemia, hyperuricemia/urate nephropathy, hyperoxaluria, hypokalemic vacuolization of PCT > DCT), then autoimmune causes (sarcoidosis, Sjogren's, IgG4) and finally CKDu.

units.title: CTID features, investigations and the CKDu concept
units.guide: CTID is asymptomatic with an insidious onset. The clinical-features table links each sign to its cause: polyuria/nocturia (concentration defect), anaemia (peritubular interstitial fibroblast EPO), nephrogenic DI (cortical collecting duct fibrosis), RTA IV (beta cell fibrosis) and RTA I (alpha intercalated cell fibrosis), with rickets in children from phosphate loss. Anaemia is maximal in CTID and minimal in ADPKD. Investigations: proteinuria <2 g/day with beta-2 microglobulin, inactive sediment, deranged RFT, small kidneys. CKDu: unknown pathophysiology, theories of heat stress, agrochemicals, fluoride, cadmium and communicable disease; eastern coast of India, middle-aged men, asymptomatic until ESRF.
